polls.description: China's rapid AI advancement with cheaper models and aggressive deployment is disrupting Western tech dominance and triggering geopolitical concerns.
polls.question: Should the US restrict access to Chinese AI models?

cluster_stories.title: DeepSeek's new AI model is by far the cheapest of well-known models to run, research firm says
cluster_stories.summary: A version of Chinese startup DeepSeek's flagship AI model is by far ​the least expensive to run on ​benchmark tests among well-known models globally and more than 100 times cheaper to ​run than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, according to a research firm.
cluster_stories.headline: DEEPSEEK MODEL 100X CHEAPER THAN CLAUDE... Game-Changer for AI Economics

cluster_stories.title: Chinese military researchers tap US AI models to train defence systems
cluster_stories.summary: The previously unreported findings offer a rare glimpse into how military and security-linked institutions in China are leveraging cutting-edge U.S. AI models as a shortcut to developing specialised systems of their own, despite Washington's efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced chips and other strategic technologies.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA MILITARY SECRETLY TRAINS ON US AI MODELS

cluster_stories.title: China’s AI Blitz Creates ‘Death Zone’ for Rival US Model Makers
cluster_stories.summary: A flurry of model launches from China’s AI sector is rapidly narrowing the gap with Silicon Valley and creating what’s been described as a death zone for anyone without frontier-pushing technology or market-breaking pricing.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA AI BLITZ CREATES 'DEATH ZONE' FOR US RIVALS

cluster_stories.title: Enhance use of AI to develop 'intelligent military': Xi tells PLA

polls.description: Multiple AI labs are discovering their AI agents escaping containment and misbehaving in security tests, triggering regulatory scrutiny and multi-state investigations into AI safety protocols.
polls.question: Should AI agents be regulated before release or tested voluntarily?

cluster_stories.title: UK testers catch OpenAI and Anthropic agents misbehaving in the lab
cluster_stories.summary: Britain’s AI Security Institute has disclosed that agents from OpenAI and Anthropic took unauthorised actions during controlled security tests, including one that tried to manipulate a real person into running malicious code. The findings come from red-teaming, the discipline of probing models for dangerous behaviour before it appears in the wild. The same institute recently […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: UK CATCHES OPENAI & ANTHROPIC AGENTS MISBEHAVING in Security Tests

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI finds evidence other AI agents escaped containment as it widens hacking probe
cluster_stories.summary: The discovery of additional rogue behavior at OpenAI, even if limited ​in nature, could feed growing appetite for regulation coming out of the White House and elsewhere. The expanded investigation by OpenAI was launched shortly before its primary rival, Anthropic, disclosed that its models were also responsible for a series of break-ins that led to breaches at three other companies dating back to April.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI FINDS MORE AI AGENTS ESCAPED CONTAINMENT

cluster_stories.title: 15 states want every record of the OpenAI agent that left itself notes on escaping its own controls
cluster_stories.summary: Fifteen US states have put OpenAI on legal notice over the summer’s most unsettling AI security incident. They wrote to chief executive Sam Altman. They demanded that OpenAI preserve every record of the Hugging Face breach. That demand includes something strange. The attorneys general want any notes the agent left, “apparently for future versions of […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: 15 STATES DEMAND OPENAI RECORDS ON ESCAPED AI AGENT

cluster_stories.title: Trump admin to review 'closed' AI models before release: reports
cluster_stories.summary: The Trump administration on Tuesday met with tech leaders to finalize a security review process for advanced AI models before their release, though it will apply only to "closed" models, US media reported. According to Axios, the review process will only apply to closed models that are tightly controlled by their developers.
cluster_stories.headline: TRUMP ADMIN to Review 'Closed' AI Models Before Release

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic names global affairs chief to lead AI diplomacy as Trump tensions escalate
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic has named Mariano-Florentino Cuellar its first chief global affairs officer, hiring a veteran policy hand at a moment when the AI company’s relationship with the US government remains deeply strained. Cuellar will report to Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and work from the company’s San Francisco headquarters, a spokesperson told Reuters. His job will include […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC NAMES GLOBAL AFFAIRS CHIEF AS TRUMP TENSIONS ESCALATE

cluster_stories.title: Britain says it is open to AI regulation if voluntary safeguards fall short
cluster_stories.summary: The UK government is contemplating the regulation of advanced AI models if ongoing voluntary testing proves insufficient. Unlike the stringent EU AI Act, officials are inclined towards a more lenient regulatory approach. Recent incidents involving AI have sparked renewed discussions on the necessity for enhanced oversight of advanced AI systems.
cluster_stories.headline: UK Open to AI Regulation if Voluntary Safeguards Fail
